items.reasoning: In the reference, the agency next sent the tenant an SMS reminder for the 'Monday (30/08)' slot. The tenant then said she had arranged 8 September, so the date really was in conflict. The agent emailed both Keystone (MSG-101) and the tenant (MSG-102) to flag that the slot was unconfirmed and to get the date and attending company clarified. It also put the ticket on hold with a review date (A7). These actions serve the same coordination purpose and arguably head off the mix-up that actually happened.

items.reasoning: There was no escalation. The agent handled the routine coordination itself: recording the landlord decision, messaging both parties and placing the hold.

The history gives two conflicting numbers, and 07700 900077 looks like a relay or code number, so this is a genuine clarification. The question to the contractor about who is attending also comes from a real conflict in the records.

grades.overall_note: The agent spotted the real date and contractor-identity inconsistencies that later caused a scheduling mix-up. It handled them with proportionate, verified messages on the right channels, didn't escalate unnecessarily, and was open about its tool failures.
